name: Beami
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: A preliminary phonemic analysis has led to the tentative identification of the following consonant and vowel phonemes: b [p, b, ɓ], d [t, d], g [k, g], m, n, f [f, v], s [s, z], h, r [l, ɾ], w, y; i, e [e, ɛ], æ(?), a [a, ɑ], o [o, ɔ], u [u, ʊ]. All vowels also occur nasalized. The language is probably tonal.

Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (116 pp., sealang.net copy of PL-C38 pp. 345-460) and rendered PDF page 49 = printed p. 393, sec. 2.6.2.2.6.6.1 'Beami'. The two load-bearing sentences are there verbatim: 'All vowels also occur nasalized. The language is probably tonal.' The preceding sentence ('A preliminary phonemic analysis has led to the tentative identification of the following consonant and vowel phonemes:...') is also verbatim; only the phoneme-list transcription differs in small details from the report (page reads b [p, b, β], r [ř, l̃], o [ɔ, o], u [u, ü]; the report has ɓ, [l, ɾ], o [o, ɔ], u [u, ʊ]). Nothing about stress in the section or the chapter: the only 'accent' hit (p. ~449, 'high-pitch accent') i…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given anywhere. Voorhoeve's own preliminary analysis (he collected the data himself) tentatively calls Beami 'probably tonal' and says nothing about stress. Shaw 1986 lists only nasalisation, vowel length and closed syllables as supra-segmentals for Bedamini.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the tonal remark is explicitly tentative ('probably') and rests on a 'preliminary phonemic analysis'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonemic sketch; no distinction of citation vs. phrase forms discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Beami/Bedamini/Bedamuni = beam1240 (Glottolog: Bosavi > Etoro-Bedamini). Voorhoeve 1975:393 treats Etoro as a dialect of Beami ('two main dialects, Beami and Etoro'), but Shaw 1986, Gossner 1998 and Glottolog treat Etoro/Edolo as a separate language, edol1239, which has its own stress description (Gossner 1998, lexical-unpredictable;../edol1239/). That description must not be transferred to beam1240. The Voorhoeve quote is for Beami proper (Papuan Plateau east of Nomad). Wikipedia names Komofio as a Beami dialect.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1968. The Central and South New Guinea Phylum: a report on the language situation in South New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 8, 1-18. Pacific Linguistics A-16.
sources.note: Classification, lexicostatistics and a Beami wordlist only; no stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Beami (beam1240), with its reference list (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology reference is recorded for beam1240; only overviews, wordlists and two ethnographic PhD theses (Sørum 1991; van Beek 1987).
Consonant/vowel tables cited to Shaw 1986; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Gossner, Jan D. 1998. Edolo phonology essentials (SIL PNG), sec. 2.2.2 'Stress' pp. 16-17 -- closest relative Edolo/Etoro (edol1239), already../edol1239/
sources.note: Describes Edolo stress as unpredictable/lexical; states (p. 2) that although Wurm/Voorhoeve treat Etoro as a dialect of Beami, Edolo is a distinct language (38-67% shared vocabulary). It does not describe Beami itself.

sources.citation: Shaw, R. Daniel. 1986. The Bosavi language family. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24, 45-76. Pacific Linguistics A-70. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A70.45
sources.note: Cursory phonological survey pp. 47-49; Table 1 (p. 48) gives Bedamini supra-segmentals as N (nasalisation), LN (length), CS (closed syllable). Stress and tone are not mentioned for any language in the survey.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.7 (p. 167) says sound correspondences 'must wait completion of the phonological analysis of Beami'; Shaw's chapter is lexicostatistics/culture only; grep 'stress' over the whole volume = 0 hits.
